title: Project-State Freshness + Authority Version-Chain Gate

source_provenance.locator: D06/D07/D08 current authority + Final Story Gate revision IDs
source_provenance.notes: Real provider revision baseline, not semantic/canon proof

problem_or_opportunity: Durable project-state coverage proves a pointer exists but does not prove that its controlling authority has not changed since the state was persisted. A stale pointer can therefore resurrect old routing even when coverage is green.
proposed_mechanism: Persist authority identity/revision observations; validate exactly one CURRENT highest-rank source with acyclic supersession lineage; compare future provider observations against baseline; return PASS_FRESH / REVIEW_REQUIRED / STALE_REBASE_REQUIRED / FAIL_CONTRACT; force re-read/reconciliation on drift without treating revision change as canon change.
expected_benefit: Closes the gap between durable pointer existence and durable pointer freshness, reducing stale continuation and accidental regression to superseded authority.
pilot_evidence: Local syntax/smoke: unchanged authority -> PASS_FRESH; revision change -> STALE_REBASE_REQUIRED
D06/D07/D08 Drive current-authority and Final Story Gate revision IDs captured directly during H17/H18 execution
red_team_findings: Revision drift does not prove semantic/canon change
Missing provider observation must be REVIEW_REQUIRED rather than assumed fresh
Provider revision identity is routing evidence only
A freshness gate must not stop dependency-independent projects when only one project is stale
next_action: Run CI; execute one unchanged real provider observation and one changed-revision rebase pilot; repeat on a second project family; then decide PILOT_PASS or repair.
notes: H17/H18 candidate. No automatic CURRENT promotion.
